title: Isandro and the Mixtape
premise: Gideon Eastwick, a seventeen-year-old coder who hides behind an anonymous account that exposes the school's rot, starts receiving handwritten notes from the legendary ghost of Ashgrove High — notes in ink that shouldn't exist, addressed to him by a name no one uses. The ghost turns out to be the residue of a student erased from school records decades ago after exposing a founder's crimes, and it can only pass on by having someone finish its unfinished accusation. As the notes pull Gideon's two identities toward collision — his anonymous exposés and his invisible real self — he discovers the beloved headmaster is the heir of the man the ghost accused, still protecting the family name. In the end Gideon chooses to sign his real name to the truth, releasing the ghost and accepting that visibility costs everything except himself.
about_author: Beatrix Thackeray is a former archivist who spent years cataloguing the unclaimed belongings of a shuttered boarding school, an experience that left her convinced every institution keeps at least one ghost. She writes young adult fiction about kids who refuse the stories adults write for them.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. We meet him counting down days to graduation while running @ashgroveleaks, an anonymous account that has just exposed a rigged scholarship. He's careful, invisible, untouchable — until he isn't. Emotional beat: the lonely comfort of being no one.

chapters.title: Ink That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A note appears inside his locker: 'Hello, Isandro.' No one calls him Isandro — that's the name only his dead mother used. The ink shimmers wrong, metallic, warm. He tells himself it's a prank. Emotional beat: a crack in the armor.

chapters.title: The Legend of Room 114
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV with best friend Priya. They dig into the school's founding myth: a student, Wren Okafor, who vanished in 1974 after accusing the Eastwick-adjacent founders of fraud. Gideon notices his own surname in the margins of the legend. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Second Note
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A second note predicts, verbatim, something Gideon will say in class the next day — before he says it. The account @ashgroveleaks gets a follower: wren_o_1974. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing he's hunted.

chapters.title: Headmaster Vale's Smile
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Headmaster Vale, charismatic and beloved, quietly buries the scholarship scandal and begins pulling records on anonymous posters. His chapters read warm but controlled. Emotional beat: charm as a weapon; the reader knows before Gideon does.

chapters.title: What Priya Saw
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She catches Gideon talking to empty air near Room 114 and confronts him; he confesses the notes. She doesn't believe in ghosts but believes in him — and offers to help trace the ink. Emotional beat: friendship as anchor.

chapters.title: The Archive Basement
chapters.summary: Gideon and Priya break into the records basement and find Wren Okafor's file surgically removed — but a carbon copy of an accusation survives, naming Aldous Vale, the founder, and implicating the current Vales. Emotional beat: history isn't past, it's hidden.

chapters.title: Isandro
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV, intimate flashback chapter. Memory of his mother, why she named him Isandro, why he buried the name when she died and his father remarried into respectability. Emotional beat: grief reframed — the ghost isn't haunting him; it's calling him home to himself.

chapters.title: The Third Note Names You
chapters.summary: A note appears on the class whiteboard in impossible ink: 'ISANDRO KNOWS.' Now the whole school speculates. Vale summons Gideon for a friendly chat that is anything but. Emotional beat: exposure without explanation — the worst kind.

chapters.title: Vale's Offer
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Vale privately offers Gideon a full ride, a future, discretion — if the leaks stop and the Okafor file stays buried. He speaks of legacy like scripture. Gideon almost says yes. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a kind face.

chapters.title: Priya Walks Away
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. She learns Gideon considered the deal and feels betrayed — not by the deal, but by his willingness to disappear again. Their fight cracks the one relationship keeping him human. Emotional beat: isolation chosen is worse than isolation imposed.

chapters.title: Room 114 at Midnight
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He finally enters Room 114 alone and meets the ghost properly: not a monster but an echo, replaying the night Wren was silenced. It shows him the truth — and shows him how little time remains before it takes him under instead. Emotional beat: terror and tenderness in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Rules of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. He decodes the pattern: the ghost can't accuse anyone itself; it needs a living voice to finish Wren's statement. But whoever finishes it becomes visible forever — and Vale's grandfather destroyed the last kid who tried. Emotional beat: understanding the price tag.

chapters.title: Ashgrove Leaks Goes Quiet
chapters.summary: Vale's POV. With the anonymous account silent, Vale relaxes — and overreaches, fast-tracking a building named for his grandfather. Meanwhile Gideon watches him from the crowd, learning how power moves when it thinks it's won. Emotional beat: the villain's fatal confidence.

chapters.title: Reconciliation in the Stacks
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Gideon finds her in the library and tells her everything — the ghost, the deal, the deadline. She doesn't forgive instantly; she chooses to help anyway, because finishing this matters more than being right. Emotional beat: repair without erasure.

chapters.title: The Ink Test
chapters.summary: Priya and Gideon analyze the ghost-ink chemically and discover it's made of ash and iron gall — literally burned records reconstituted. Every note is written in what was destroyed. Emotional beat: proof that erasure never actually works.

chapters.title: Seventeen Days
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The ghost's presence begins bleeding into him — lost hours, handwriting that isn't his, Wren's memories surfacing. Graduation is seventeen days away, and so is the point of no return. Emotional beat: a countdown with teeth.

chapters.title: What Vale Buried
chapters.summary: Dual POV climax setup. Gideon and Priya locate the original evidence Wren hid — in the cornerstone of the new Vale building, about to be sealed behind concrete forever. Vale, tipped off, waits for them there. Emotional beat: converging lines, held breath.

chapters.title: The Cornerstone
chapters.summary: Climax, Gideon's POV. Confrontation in the construction site: Vale offers everything one last time, then threatens expulsion, ruin, his father's career. Gideon opens the cornerstone, holds the truth in his hands, and — live-streaming under his own face, not an avatar — says his name aloud: 'I'm Isandro Eastwick, and here is what your family buried.' Emotional beat: the terrifying freedom of being seen.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Name
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The recording detonates across the school and beyond; Vale suspends Gideon pending investigation, but the board — and Wren's surviving family — mobilize. Gideon faces his father, who finally hears the name Isandro and flinches, then listens. Emotional beat: consequences arriving honestly.

chapters.title: Wren's Last Page
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. In Room 114, Gideon reads aloud the final paragraph of Wren's accusation, completing what was interrupted fifty years ago. The ink goes cold, then ordinary. The room is just a room. Somewhere, a debt is paid. Emotional beat: release — quiet, enormous.

chapters.title: Signed, Isandro
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Gideon's POV. Graduation day: Vale resigned under investigation, Wren Okafor's name restored to the honor roll, a new plaque in Room 114. Gideon publishes one last post — no handle, just his name — and walks across the stage as himself. Emotional beat: invisibility traded, gladly, for a self worth seeing.
